pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the URL Shortener project: its purpose, architectural evolution (Section 1 through to and including Section 4), key design goals, and a map to all child pages.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for setting up the project locally: cloning the repo, configuring environment variables via .env, installing dependencies, and running the app with Docker Compose or directly with uvicorn.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Describes the three-tier architecture (FastAPI app + PostgreSQL + Redis), the dual-engine design, the cache-aside pattern, and the write-decoupling strategy. Links to deeper child pages for each subsystem.

pages.title: Core Application
pages.purpose: Overview of the application source code in app/, covering the API layer, data models, and the Redis cache abstraction. Links to child pages for each major component.

pages.title: API Endpoints
pages.purpose: Detailed reference for every FastAPI endpoint: POST /shorten, GET /{short_code}, GET /stats/{short_code}, DELETE /{short_code}, and GET /health. Covers request/response schemas, status codes, URL normalization, and collision-retry logic.

pages.title: Data Models
pages.purpose: Documents the SQLAlchemy ORM model (Code / codes table), Pydantic schemas (URLRequest, URLResponse, StatsResponse), and the deliberate separation between validation and persistence layers.

pages.title: Redis Cache Layer
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the RedisCache class in app/cache.py: its methods (get, set, delete, exists, increment, get_int, keys), TTL semantics, the two key namespaces (short_code mappings vs. clicks: counters), and how it is wired into main.py.

pages.title: Background Processing & Sync
pages.purpose: Explains the two async mechanisms: FastAPI BackgroundTasks for per-request click increments (increment_click), and the daemon thread running sync_to_db every 30 seconds via the every() helper. Covers the dual-engine isolation strategy (engine vs. sync_engine) and eventual-consistency guarantees.

pages.title: Testing
pages.purpose: Overview of the test suite structure, tooling choices (pytest, fakeredis, TestClient), and the test categories. Links to child pages for API tests, cache integration tests, and read-replica isolation tests.

pages.title: API Endpoint Tests
pages.purpose: Documents tests/test_api_endpoints.py: the five test phases (Repository Setup, Core Endpoints, Unit Tests, Deployment, Load Testing), the setup_db fixture, SQLite test database strategy, and key assertions for each endpoint.

pages.title: Cache Integration Tests
pages.purpose: Documents tests/test_cache_integration.py: use of fakeredis for isolation, test classes covering basic operations, TTL expiry, URL caching use cases, click counter scenarios, cache-aside pattern verification, error handling, and memory management.

pages.title: Read Replica Tests
pages.purpose: Documents tests/test_read_replica.py: the five test classes (ReplicaSetup, WritesGoToPrimary, ReadsGoToReplica, ReplicationLag, PrimaryReplicaIsolation), the sync_replica helper that simulates WAL replication, and the client_with_replica fixture that patches both engines. Covers eventual-consistency assertions and the 404-before-sync behaviour.

pages.title: Infrastructure & Deployment
pages.purpose: Overview of how the service is containerized and deployed, both locally via Docker Compose and on AWS. Links to child pages for Docker setup, CI/CD pipeline, and AWS architecture.

pages.title: Docker & Docker Compose
pages.purpose: Covers the Dockerfile (python:3.11-slim base, uvicorn entrypoint), docker-compose.yml service definitions (app, db, redis), environment variables, named volumes (postgres_data, redis-data), health checks, and the depends_on startup sequencing.

pages.title: CI/CD Pipeline
pages.purpose: Documents the GitHub Actions workflow (run-urlshortener): the four sequential jobs (flake8-lint → check_requirements → test → docker), service sidecar containers for PostgreSQL and Redis, pip-tools dependency validation, and the Docker health-check retry loop.

pages.title: AWS Architecture
pages.purpose: Documents the production AWS deployment described in docs/AWS_ARCHITECTURE.md: EC2 application layer (t3.small × 2), RDS PostgreSQL primary + read replica (db.t4g.micro), ElastiCache Valkey, Application Load Balancer, connection pool math across instances, and the request flow for each endpoint type.

pages.title: Load Testing & Performance Results
pages.purpose: Overview of the Locust-based load testing setup and the visual performance artifacts across all four sections of architectural evolution. Links to child pages for the Locust configuration and the benchmark results.

pages.title: Locust Load Test Configuration
pages.purpose: Documents locustfile.py: the URLShortenerUser class, task weights (create_short_url:2, redirect:7, get_stats:1), wait_time settings, the uuid4-per-request strategy for honest write-path testing, and how to run Locust against the service.

pages.title: Performance Benchmarks & Visual Results
pages.purpose: Presents the load test results across all sections: Section 1 (synchronous monolith, 108 RPS), Section 2 (Redis + BackgroundTasks, 327.8 RPS), Section 3 (read replica added), and Section 4 (AWS deployment, 715–734 RPS at 1000–2000 concurrent users). Covers the throughput improvements, latency comparisons, failure rates, and the stored PNG artifacts (tables and graphs) for each section.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Definitions of all codebase-specific terms, abbreviations, and domain concepts an onboarding engineer needs to know, each with code pointers. Covers terms from all four architectural sections including AWS-specific terminology added in Section 4.
